Referred Sections: Radiation Oncology Guidelines For Special Techniques > Brachytherapy of the Coronary Arteries (TOC: S3.5)
Radiation Oncology Guidelines For Special Techniques > Brachytherapy of the Coronary Arteries > DISCUSSION (TOC: S3.5.3)

Required findings: Patient has a history of percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) with placement of a stent.
Patient experiences in-stent restenosis (ISR) within the native coronary artery or saphenous vein graft (SVG).
The ISR is confirmed by diagnostic imaging such as intravascular ultrasound (IVUS) or computed tomography angiography (CTA), or by clinical symptoms suggestive of recurrent ischemia.
Conservative management including medical therapy and/or repeat balloon angioplasty has failed to resolve the restenosis.
Patient is not a candidate for repeat drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation due to factors such as lesion location, patient characteristics, or inability to adhere to dual antiplatelet therapy.
Patient is not a candidate for bypass surgery.

Non-Indications: Treatment of new stenosis of native coronary arteries or saphenous vein grafts.
Restenosis of native coronary arteries or saphenous vein grafts at the unstented site of a previous PCI.
Primary prevention of restenosis after stent implantation for de novo lesions.
Important criteria & exceptions: Brachytherapy may be considered in patients with recurrent ISR who are not candidates for repeat DES or bypass surgery.
A prolonged intake of clopidogrel for 1 year after radiation is necessary.
Documentation required: Patient medical history including prior PCI and stent placement.
Prior imaging studies (e.g., CTA, IVUS) demonstrating the presence and extent of in-stent restenosis.
Clinical notes documenting failed conservative management attempts.
Provider documentation outlining patient's inability to receive repeat DES or bypass surgery.
